title: Hop-by-hop verification stream with sampling controls for routing observability
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Existing routing observability surfaces either store full decision traces (high cost and storage) or emit only final route indices (low debug value). When incidents occur where an upstream policy or regional fallback influenced latency or model quality, engineers lack a compact, replayable record that ties per-hop policy checks, model variant selections, and measured latencies into a verifiable sequence.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, append-only "Hop Verification Stream" that records per-hop decision artifacts (policy match id, decision outcome, selected model variant, per-hop latency and queue time, reason codes, and sample of request metadata) with tunable sampling and retention controls. The stream should support: fast lookups for recent failures, compact export for offline replay, and integration into Console incident dashboards.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change routing decision logic, global sampling of user payloads, or add long-term archival analytics pipelines (those are separate projects).

Why unique: Instead of full fidelity traces we will record a canonical verification record per request path that is sufficient to reproduce routing choices without storing entire request bodies. We will add sampling controls at three levels: 1) deterministic sampling for errors and high-latency requests, 2) probabilistic sampling for normal traffic, and 3) targeted capture for flagged customers or routes.

Privacy & security: Verification records must avoid PII. Fields that could be sensitive (prompt prefixes, user identifiers) will be hashed or replaced with tokenized references. Security review is required because records may be surfaced in support tools and exported for incident analysis.
acceptance_criteria: A new Hop Verification Stream is produced for all routed requests with the agreed schema (policy_id, hop_index, outcome, model_variant, latency_ms, queue_ms, reason_code, sample_id, hashed_request_ref)
Sampling controls implemented: error-triggered capture, probabilistic capture with configurable p in Console, and customer/route-based forced capture
Storage overhead measured: end-to-end 99th percentile additional p99 overhead per request < 2ms; storage growth estimated for p=0.01 and p=0.1 scenarios documented
Console view: incident timeline can display per-hop verification entries for a request id and link back to raw trace where available
Exports: CLI tool can export a compact replay bundle (verification records + small reference map) for offline replay in staging
Privacy: verification records do not contain raw prompts or raw user identifiers; an automated review checklist signed off by Security
End-to-end test coverage and a load test showing stable behavior at 2x normal traffic for p=0.01 sampling
implementation_notes: Schema: flat key-value schema optimized for columnar storage. Use single-line JSON records written to a Kafka topic 'hop-verif-v1' for downstream consumers.
Encoding: keep records small (~300 bytes avg) by using short reason codes and integer IDs for policy/model references. Use base64 where necessary for small binary blobs.
Sampling hooks: integrate sampling decisions into the routing layer before any model-heavy work to avoid added compute on unsampled requests.
Privacy: implement a hashing utility (salted, per-tenant) for request references and enforce a scrubber that strips any headers flagged by privacy team.
Console: add a 'Verification' tab in request detail view with pagination and a compact per-hop table (hop index, decision, variant, latency, reason).
Storage & retention: default retention 30 days for probabilistic captures, 90 days for error-triggered captures. Provide admin controls for enterprise customers.
Cost trade-off: default sampling p=0.01 to balance debug signal vs storage costs; run experiments to tune after 4 weeks of telemetry.
Backward compatibility: older routers will emit a minimal compatibility envelope; new SDKs will surface the full per-hop record. Plan a 6-week dual-write period for migration.
progress_updates: 2025-03-10: RFC drafted and reviewed with Runtime and Observability teams. Initial schema proposed.
2025-03-12: Prototype topic created in staging Kafka and a small producer added to the region router. Verified low overhead at 100rps.
2025-03-14: Security reviewed initial schema; requested removal of any un-hashed session tokens and addition of per-tenant salt. Implemented change and resubmitted.
2025-03-15: Console wireframe for Verification tab reviewed by PM (Mariana Lopez) and Design (Evelyn Park). Minor UX changes suggested (add filtering by reason_code and hop_index).
comments: Mariana Lopez (PM) - 2025-03-11: Strong need from two enterprise customers for faster RCA on cross-region fallbacks; prioritize error-triggered captures.
Evelyn Park (Design) - 2025-03-13: Keep the console view compact; engineers want an export button. Also include a copyable 'replay bundle' id.
Rajiv Malhotra (SRE) - 2025-03-14: Ensure sampling decision is deterministic when using client-side request id to allow correlating with other traces.
Security Team (notes) - 2025-03-14: Must add per-tenant salt rotation plan and a toggle to disable verification stream for customers with strict data contracts.
